$comment: 0.8.0 catalog. Two rules: (1) a workload used to judge a Cloudflare IP must actually be served by Cloudflare, otherwise it measures somebody else's CDN; (2) a streaming ladder can never prove more quality than its own top rendition, so every entry declares ladderMaxMbps and the probe caps the reported quality by it.

browsing.name: cloudflare-docs
browsing.description: Cloudflare developer docs: served by Cloudflare, many small same-origin assets, stable markup - the closest thing to a normal content page on this edge

browsing.name: cloudflare-blog
browsing.description: Cloudflare blog home: image-heavy page on Cloudflare, exercises larger objects and image resizing on the same edge

browsing.name: cloudflare-speed
browsing.description: Cloudflare speed landing page, same origin as the load endpoints

browsing.name: cdnjs
browsing.description: cdnjs library index on cdnjs.cloudflare.com: pure static asset delivery from Cloudflare, no application server in the path

browsing.name: wikipedia
browsing.description: CONTROL ONLY (not Cloudflare): use to compare the tunnel itself against the Cloudflare edge, never to rank Cloudflare IPs

streaming.name: apple-advanced-hevc
streaming.description: Apple advanced reference stream (fMP4, HEVC + H.264 ladder, byte-range init maps). Real multi-rendition ABR ladder up to 1080p, which is what ordinary playback looks like

streaming.name: apple-4k-dolby
streaming.description: Apple advanced 4K Dolby Vision / Atmos reference ladder. The only default workload whose top rendition is high enough to honestly demonstrate 4K capability

streaming.name: mux-test-hls
streaming.description: Mux public HLS test stream, widely used reference ladder up to 1080p

streaming.name: bitmovin-sintel
streaming.description: Bitmovin Sintel demo ladder on their current CDN host

streaming.name: akamai-bbb-low
streaming.description: Low-bitrate Big Buck Bunny ladder (max ~1.5 Mbps): useful on very constrained paths where richer ladders never start playback
